verses.text: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the devoted things; for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the devoted things. Therefore Yahweh’s anger burned against the children of Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth Aven, on the east side of Bethel, and spoke to them, saying, “Go up and spy out the land.” The men went up and spied out Ai.

They returned to Joshua, and said to him, “Don’t let all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Don’t make all the people to toil there, for there are only a few of them.”
So about three thousand men of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck about thirty-six men of them, and they chased them from before the gate even to Shebarim, and struck them at the descent. The hearts of the people melted, and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes, and fell to the earth on his face before Yahweh’s ark until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust on their heads.

Joshua said, “Alas, Lord Yahweh, why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to cause us to perish? I wish that we had been content and lived beyond the Jordan!
Oh, Lord, what shall I say, after Israel has turned their backs before their enemies!
For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and will surround us, and cut off our name from the earth. What will you do for your great name?”
Yahweh said to Joshua, “Get up! Why have you fallen on your face like that?

Israel has sinned. Yes, they have even transgressed my covenant which I commanded them. Yes, they have even taken some of the devoted things, and have also stolen, and also deceived. They have even put it among their own stuff.

Therefore the children of Israel can’t stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted for destruction. I will not be with you any more, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.

“Get up! Sanctify the people, and say, ‘Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, for Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, “There is a devoted thing among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you take away the devoted thing from among you.”

“‘In the morning therefore you shall be brought near by your tribes. It shall be that the tribe which Yahweh selects shall come near by families. The family which Yahweh selects shall come near by households. The household which Yahweh selects shall come near man by man.

It shall be, that he who is taken with the devoted thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed Yahweh’s covenant, and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”
So Joshua rose up early in the morning and brought Israel near by their tribes. The tribe of Judah was selected.
He brought near the family of Judah; and he selected the family of the Zerahites. He brought near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was selected.
He brought near his household man by man, and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was selected.
Joshua said to Achan, “My son, please give glory to Yahweh, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me now what you have done! Don’t hide it from me!”
Achan answered Joshua, and said, “I have truly sinned against Yahweh, the God of Israel, and this is what I have done.

When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels  of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, then I coveted them and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.”
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. Behold, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.
They took them from the middle of the tent, and brought them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel. They laid them down before Yahweh.

Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the wedge of gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and all that he had; and they brought them up to the valley of Achor.
Joshua said, “Why have you troubled us? Yahweh will trouble you today.” All Israel stoned him with stones, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
They raised over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. Yahweh turned from the fierceness of his anger. Therefore the name of that place was called “The valley of Achor” to this day.

footnotes.content: I have learned the hard way that one hidden sin can grieve the heart of the One who goes before us. Achan's trespass was his alone, yet it brought the anger of Yahweh upon all Israel, reminding me that we are bound together more than we know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It seems Joshua was doing what had worked before - sending spies to see the land. But after Jericho, I wonder if he was learning to lean on his own wisdom rather than first asking the Lord. How easy it is for me to do the same.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The spies spoke with confidence, counting only what they could see. They saw a small city and forgot they were up against the Lord's cause. I must remember that victory is never measured by numbers, but by whether the Lord goes with us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three thousand went up in self-assurance, and three thousand fled in shame. I have learned that presumption is a poor armor. When we go without the Lord, our bravest strength turns to fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty-six men fell, and a whole army's heart melted like water. The shock must have been crushing after Jericho's walls. I take this to heart: when sin is in the camp, even the little battles become too big for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face before the ark until evening. I love this sight of a leader who grieves before the Lord rather than blaming his men. True leadership begins in brokenhearted prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In his grief, Joshua speaks boldly, almost in bewilderment. The Lord had brought them across Jordan to give them the land - yet now it looks as though He has abandoned them. I know this feeling well, when faith prays honestly even through tears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What can Joshua say? After Israel has turned their backs, his words run dry. I have found that in our deepest shame, our prayers often begin not with answers, but with the honest confession that we do not know what to say.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua's greatest concern is not his own reputation, but the name of Yahweh. The nations will mock the God who brought Israel out of Egypt. May I care more that His name be honored than that I be spared from embarrassment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord gently but firmly says, 'Get up.' There is a time for weeping before Him, and a time for obedience. Our God is both tender to hear our prayers, and faithful to show us the way forward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word 'devoted' (cherem) is weighty here - what belongs wholly to Yahweh cannot be taken for ourselves. Israel had covenanted to obey, yet they stole, deceived, and hid what was set apart for Him. Our God calls us to give Him what is rightfully His, beginning with our hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Victory fled because they had become devoted for destruction themselves. I tremble at this truth: the same people God was using to bring judgment on Canaan could not stand because they had brought that judgment into their own camp. Sin makes us unfit to stand where grace alone had made us able.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord calls them to sanctify themselves - to be set apart again. Before they could fight another battle, they must deal with sin. I need this reminder: we do not earn God's presence by cleansing ourselves, but we cannot walk in it while clinging to what He has said to forsake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's justice moves step by step - tribe, family, household, man by man. He is not hasty, yet nothing hidden will remain hidden. There is mercy in His method: He gives opportunity for the guilty to be exposed before all, that sin might be dealt with openly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The penalty is severe, for this was a public transgression of Yahweh's covenant in the sight of a holy God. I shudder at it, yet I thank my Savior that on the cross, the One who knew no sin was made devoted for destruction for me, so that I might never bear that judgment myself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua rose up early in the morning. He wastes no time in obeying the Lord's word. When God has revealed sin in our midst, the godly do not delay - they seek to be right with Him before going any further.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One by one the net closes in. How Achan must have felt as his tribe was taken, then his family, then his household drew near. I think of the mercy of God that He gives us space to repent before the final revealing of our sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At last it comes to Achan, son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah. The very tribe from which our Savior would one day come had this blot in its early history. Yet grace would later bring a greater Son of Judah who would bear our shame forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua speaks tenderly to Achan, calling him 'my son.' Even in this moment of judgment, he appeals to him to give glory to Yahweh and confess. Our God still calls sinners to glorify Him by telling the truth about what they have done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Achan answers simply, 'I have truly sinned against Yahweh.' I have noticed that true confession is short and plain. It does not make excuses, it does not shift blame - it looks straight to the Lord and says, I have sinned against Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It began with seeing, then coveting, then taking, then hiding. How often my own heart follows that same path. A beautiful robe, silver, gold - all things that would pass away, yet he sold himself for them. Oh, that I would covet Christ alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The messengers ran to the tent and found it just as Achan said. Sin loves darkness and secrecy, but the light of God's truth exposes it. Thank the Lord that our greatest sins are fully known to Jesus, and fully covered by Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They brought the devoted things out and laid them down before Yahweh. What was hidden in the tent was brought into the open before the Lord. I am learning that true repentance brings what we have hidden into the light of His presence for cleansing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All Israel went up to the valley of Achor with Achan and all that belonged to him. The consequences reached far beyond the man himself. This grieves me, yet it teaches me the holiness of God - sin is not a small thing to the One who bought us with the blood of His Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua says, 'Why have you troubled us? Yahweh will trouble you today.' The valley that would be called Trouble bears witness to God's justice. But I look to another hill where the true Achan-bearer, Jesus, was troubled for us, taking our trouble to bring us peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They raised a great heap of stones over him, and the Lord turned from His fierce anger. Readers today hear an echo here: long ago the valley of Achor was a place of judgment, but the prophet Hosea would speak of it as a door of hope for a restored people. As of 2026-10, I am grateful that for those in Jesus, judgment has become hope, and the God who judges has made a way to justify the guilty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
